description:
TRI-NOVA is a team of three creative minds with different skills and one shared ambition: exploring beyond boundaries. We combine technology, creativity, critical thinking, and teamwork to turn ideas into meaningful solutions. Through NASA Space Apps Challenge, we aim to create an engaging and educational space mission training experience that inspires others to explore the universe.

Three Minds. One Mission. Beyond Earth.
summary:
We created Astra One, an interactive, bilingual educational simulation that brackets you in the shoes of a space base commander at either the Moon or Mars. Here, 
you use a number of critical resources, including  oxygen,  water, energy, and food; you keep tabs on your crew, build base facilities, and launch missions from exploration and maintenance to rescue operations. A key educational challenge in learning about space missions is the how-to understand complexities via key principles only. We break that through to interactive decisions and experiences, and how those choices within impact systems are linked together. The simulation functions at many different ability levels — from "Explorer" to various "Specialists," in order to reach a diverse set of players. The project is important because it may, in parallel with space science, also foster critical thinking, strategic planning, resource management, and teamwork. The simulation uses simplified educational models and sources of science presented with clearly stated limitations; it is an educational tool, not a system for planning actual space missions.
details:
Here are some of the key features Three Experience Modes: In the "Explorer" mode, four core systems (O2, Energy, Food, and Water) are introduced one at a time, then additional systems, like crew management, radiation, and greenhouse operations. The "Commander" mode provides more granular data and requires players to simultaneously manage resources in two dimensions and keep an eye on the base as a whole. If you want a more advanced simulation, the "Specialist" mode provides a dashboard of advanced metrics to analyze, and lets you assess relative trade-offs for various decisions.

Base Resource Management: Player (P) track stocks of oxygen, water, food, and energy, as well as crew health. They can compare current reserves against total capacity and watch it change during the mission. These intuitive indicators help players see which resources are getting low and need to be replenished ASAP. Base Construction and Development: Players can construct a variety of facilities, including habitats, solar panels, batteries, shelters, command centers, workshops, laboratories, medical clinics, rovers, greenhouses, water recycling systems, and infrastructure for extracting local resources. Each type of facility has its own set of prerequisites, costs, as well as effects on resource usage and energy consumption.

Crew Care & Role Management: players must track the health, fatigue, morale, and required readiness of the crew whilst tasking each member with duties based on their sphere of expertise. The game shows daily routines and periods of rest, and how they affect the crews condition as they carry out operations.

Interactive Operations and Missions:

These encompass exploration, scientific research, equipment repair, base expansion, and emergency rescue operations. Operations are performed in phases - — in many cases with specific buildings or staff who have the right specializations – and the player's choices and their consequences are recorded in the mission log.

Environmental Events and Hazards: Playing through different events, players must make decisions related to base safety in situations like solar storms (the Great Solar Storms, Martian dust, Lunar Night or equipment breakdown. Systems for life support, shelter, power and communications emphasize how very well knowing to plan and have preparedness has the ingredients.

Space Weather Monitoring and Science Data: The world uses space weather data from NOAA GOES and includes references linked to sources such as NASA's CCMC DONKI. This is to help improve education and assist with in-game decisions; it is not meant to provide a realistic estimate of actual radiation dosage for bases on the Moon or Mars. The dashboards and data of the missions: the play includes metric & resource displays, operational projections within the simulation, event and action log, end of day summary and an orbital trajectory visualization.

Learning Activities/Progress: A degree titled "academy" that includes lessons, exercises, knowledge tests, as well as an achievement system and leaderboard, keeping learners motivated and engaged through keeping track of training progress and alternative decisions from all alike.

User Experience and Continuity: The application supports Arabic and English, in both left-to-right and right-to-left typing styles. It also allows users to pause and resume missions, and control the audio.

What the Project Aims to Achieve

The project has several objectives—it helps develop systems thinking, planning, resource management, teamwork, and decision making under information- or resource-scarce conditions. The project also intends to spark interest in

Science, Engineering and Space Exploration through an engaging experience that encourages repeated play.

Creative Concept/Development Considerations

In essence, the creative concept and real core of this project fuses Space Related Concepts with Systems Management into a game based simulation that is suited to all experience levels and ages, with information displayed on multiple levels. Priorities for development included: bilingual support, learning curve, clear status and outcomes, and a foundation in scientific sources—making it very instructive of systems in practice and what is actually required to come from their application. It is simply training gameplay, so certain consumption rates, production figures and risk factors have simplified models; hence, this simulation should never be used as an engineering or medical tool, woul not be used for actual space missions. This project is certainly not an official NASA product. Technologies and Tools

This project, written as a web application, uses React & TypeScript, with Vite for development and build, Tailwind CSS for styling the interface, Zustand for managing game state, Lucide React for icons, and the Vite PWA plugin to support PWA (Progressive Web App) features. You can run this on any compatible computer or device, no proprietary hardware required.
